auth.signInLead: Welcome back to your glaze notebook.
auth.keepLead: Keep everything you made as {name}: add your email and a password. It stays free.
auth.signUpLead: Free. Your recipes, materials and notes are kept private to your account.
auth.trialNote: Already have an account? Signing in brings what you made as {name} into it. New here? <signup>Create an account</signup> to keep it instead.
auth.keepSignedIn: Keep me signed in on this device
auth.privacy: Your email and what you save are used only to run your account, and are stored with Amazon Web Services in the US. <privacy>How Glazecalc handles your data</privacy>
auth.dataNotice: Glazecalc is a free, open-source project, and accounts are kept on servers in the United States. You can read the guides and try the calculator without an account, or run your own copy. Whether to create an account here is your own decision, and the project accepts no responsibility for it. <where>Where your account is kept, and your choice</where>
auth.signUpFailed: Error: could not create the account.
auth.passkeyHint: A passkey uses your fingerprint, face or screen lock instead of a password. Add one on your account page.

secondStep.heading: Two-step sign-in
secondStep.signingInAs: Your password is right. One more step to sign in as {email}.
secondStep.leadCode: Open your authenticator app and enter the code it shows for Glazecalc.
secondStep.leadPasskey: Use your passkey to finish signing in.
secondStep.leadRecovery: Enter one of the recovery codes you saved when you turned on two-step sign-in. Each code works once.
secondStep.codeHint: {digits} digits. A new code shows every 30 seconds.
secondStep.codeFormat: Enter the {digits}-digit code from your authenticator app.
secondStep.recoveryMissing: Enter one of your recovery codes.
secondStep.noPasskeysHere: This browser cannot use passkeys. Use another way below, or sign in on a device that can.
secondStep.reloadNote: This step waits {minutes} minutes. If you leave or reload this page, you will need to enter your password again.
secondStep.expired: Signing in took too long. Please enter your password again.

passkey.cancelled: The passkey was not used: the request was cancelled or timed out, or this device has no passkey for Glazecalc. Please try again, or use another way.
passkey.registered: This passkey is already on your account.
passkey.browserFailed: This browser could not use the passkey. Please try again, or use another way.

forgot.heading: Reset your password
forgot.checkInbox: Check your inbox and junk folder. If nothing arrives, check the address and ask again.
forgot.intro: Enter the email for your account, and we will send you a link to choose a new password.
forgot.failed: Error: could not send the reset email. Please try again.

reset.heading: Choose a new password
reset.incomplete: This page needs the link from a password reset email, and this one is incomplete.
reset.hint: At least 8 characters. Every device signed in to the account will be signed out.
reset.failed: Error: could not change the password. Please try again.
reset.secondStep: If your account uses two-step sign-in, you will still need your authenticator app, a passkey or a recovery code to sign in.

account.keepText: This trial and everything in it are removed on {date}. Create a free account to keep them: your recipes, materials and notes stay just as they are, and {name} stays your display name.
account.title: Your account
account.passwordHint: At least 8 characters. Other devices signed in to this account will be signed out.
account.changeFailed: Error: could not change the password. Please try again.
account.deleteText: This removes your account and everything you saved: recipes, materials, additives, notes, firing logs and advice. It cannot be undone.
account.deleteFailed: Error: could not delete the account. Please try again.
account.unverifiedText: We sent a link to {email} when you made this account. Open it to confirm that the address is yours. Until then we send mail to it only when you ask, such as a password reset.
account.resendFailed: Error: could not send the link. Please try again.
account.emailText: We send a link to the new address, and your email changes when you open it. We also tell your current address. Every device signed in to this account will be signed out.
account.emailFailed: Error: could not send the link. Please try again.
account.signOutText: Signs you out on every device, this one included. Use it if you lost a device or think someone else has your sign-in.
account.signOutFailed: Error: could not sign out. Please try again.
account.confirmStep: Two-step sign-in is on, so confirm it is you: your password and a second step.

mfa.heading: Two-step sign-in
mfa.intro: Ask for a second step when you sign in, as well as your password: a code from an authenticator app, or a passkey. Then someone who learns your password still cannot get in.
mfa.loadFailed: Could not load your two-step sign-in. Please reload the page.
mfa.onText: You sign in with your password and a second step, or with a passkey alone.
mfa.offText: To turn it on, set up an authenticator app or add a passkey.
mfa.confirmEmailFirst: Confirm your email first, above. We use it to tell you about changes to how you sign in, and to help if you lose your second step.
mfa.appText: An app on your phone or in your password manager shows a new code every 30 seconds, to enter when you sign in.
mfa.passkeysText: A passkey signs you in with your fingerprint, face or screen lock, on this device or your phone. It can be your second step, or sign you in on its own, without your password.
mfa.noPasskeysHere: This browser cannot make or use passkeys. Try another browser or device.
mfa.name: Name for the passkey
mfa.nameHint: So you can tell your passkeys apart, such as "Laptop" or "Phone".
mfa.nameCheck: Give the passkey a name of 1 to {most} characters.
mfa.passkeyLimit: You have {most} passkeys, the most an account can have. Remove one to add another.
mfa.codesLeft: {count, plural, one {# of {total} recovery codes left.} other {# of {total} recovery codes left.}} If you cannot use your app or a passkey, a code signs you in instead. Each code works once.
mfa.codesLow: Make new codes soon. If they run out and you lose your app and passkeys, you cannot sign in.
mfa.offWhat: Two-step sign-in stays on while you have an authenticator app or a passkey. Removing the last of them turns it off, and then:
mfa.offPassword: Signing in needs only your password, so anyone who learns it can sign in.
mfa.offSignOut: Every other device signed in to your account is signed out. This one stays signed in.
mfa.offEmail: We email you that it was turned off.
mfa.offRemoveApp: Turn off two-step sign-in (removes the app)
mfa.offRemoveAppFirst: Remove the app, to start turning it off
mfa.offPasskeys: {count, plural, one {To turn it off, remove your passkey under Passkeys, above.} other {To turn it off, remove your # passkeys under Passkeys, above.}}
mfa.offPasskeysToo: {count, plural, one {You also have a passkey: remove it under Passkeys, above, as well as the app.} other {You also have # passkeys: remove them under Passkeys, above, as well as the app.}}
mfa.addAppText: To set up an authenticator app, first confirm it is you.
mfa.removeAppText: To remove the authenticator app, confirm it is you.
mfa.addPasskeyText: Name the passkey and confirm it is you. Then your browser asks you to make the passkey.
mfa.removePasskeyText: To remove the passkey "{name}", confirm it is you.
mfa.newCodesText: New codes replace your old ones, which stop working. Confirm it is you.
mfa.lastFactor: This is your last second step, so two-step sign-in turns off and your recovery codes stop working.
mfa.passkeyNext: Your browser asks for your passkey when you continue.
mfa.passkeyReadyText: Thank you. Now make the passkey "{name}": when you press the button, your browser asks for your fingerprint, face or screen lock, or for your phone. If it does not work, you can try again for {minutes} minutes without confirming again.
mfa.failed: Error: could not make the change. Please try again.
mfa.setupOpen: Open your authenticator app and choose to add an account.
mfa.setupScan: Scan this QR code with the app, or type in the key.
mfa.setupTap: Tap the button to add Glazecalc to an authenticator app or password manager on this phone.
mfa.showQr: Show the QR code, to set it up on another device
mfa.setupScanOther: Scan it with the authenticator app on the other device.
mfa.qrAlt: QR code for adding Glazecalc to an authenticator app
mfa.openInApp: Add to an authenticator app on this device
mfa.clipboardNote: Copied text can stay in your clipboard history and reach your other devices. Paste it straight into your password manager, then clear your clipboard history.
mfa.setupCode: Enter the {digits}-digit code the app now shows for Glazecalc
mfa.codesText: Keep these somewhere safe, such as your password manager, or print them and keep them with your papers. If you cannot use your app or a passkey, a code signs you in instead. Each code works once. They are shown only now.
mfa.printNote: Each code works once. Keep this page somewhere safe.
mfa.copyFailed: Could not copy. Please select the text and copy it.
mfa.fileNote: Each code works once. Keep this file somewhere safe.

export.heading: Download my data
export.text: Save a copy of everything your account holds as one file: your details, settings, materials on hand, recipes, materials, additives, notes, firing logs, advice and trash. It does not include your password. Keep the file somewhere private, because it holds all you saved.
export.csvText: Or save a spreadsheet of just your recipes or just your own materials, to open in Excel, Numbers or Sheets.

settings.heading: Settings
settings.intro: Saved with your account, so they hold on every device.
settings.saveFailed: The setting could not be saved. Please try again.

language.help: The language of the app, the guides and your emails. Changing it opens this page in that language.

none.label: Not chosen
none.saved: Saved: no region chosen; defaults follow your browser.

region.help: The materials sold there, and the defaults for numbers, dates, temperatures and cones below. Until you choose, they follow your browser's language.

auto.label: As my language and region
auto.saved: Saved: numbers and dates as your language and region write them.

format.saved: Saved: numbers and dates as in {language}.
format.help: How numbers and dates are written: 12,345.6 or 12.345,6, and the order of day and month.

either.label: A comma or a point for decimals
either.saved: Saved: amounts can be typed with a comma or a point.

comma.label: A comma for decimals
comma.saved: Saved: amounts are typed with a comma for decimals.

point.label: A point for decimals
point.saved: Saved: amounts are typed with a point for decimals.

decimalMark.help: With either, an amount such as 1,250 is read the way your numbers are written above.

temperature.help: Until you choose, this follows your region: °F in the United States, °C elsewhere.

temperature.label: By temperature, as a kiln controller's program

cones.help: Until you choose, this follows your region: Orton cones in the US, UK, Ireland, Australia and New Zealand, SK cones in Japan, temperature in the rest of Europe.

sg.label: Specific gravity
sg.saved: Saved: glaze density as specific gravity.

baume.label: Degrees Baumé, from a hydrometer
baume.saved: Saved: glaze density in degrees Baumé.

pint.label: Pint weight, the ounces in an imperial pint
pint.saved: Saved: glaze density as pint weight.

density.help: How the guides give the thickness of a glaze. Until you choose, this follows your region: degrees Baumé in Italy and Japan, specific gravity elsewhere.

system.label: As this device is set
system.saved: Saved: light or dark as each device is set.

theme.help: Printed recipes are always black on white.

palette.help: For buttons, links and tabs, named for glazes. Each is easy to read in light and in dark.

grams.label: Grams
grams.saved: Saved: batch weights are in grams.

pounds.label: Pounds and ounces
pounds.saved: Saved: batch weights are in pounds and ounces.

single.label: To a tenth of a gram
single.saved: Saved: grams show to a tenth.

full.label: Full precision
full.saved: Saved: grams show in full, to 5 decimal places.

gramPrecision.help: To a tenth, amounts under 10 g still show hundredths (2.35 g), for colorants in small test batches.

off.label: Off: never add lead to a recipe or suggest it
off.saved: Saved: lead is never added to a recipe or suggested.

on.label: On: materials with lead can be added and suggested
on.saved: Saved: materials with lead can be added and suggested.

lead.help: Lead is poisonous to breathe or swallow and builds up in the body, and a lead glaze can release it into food and drink; no calculation can tell whether a fired piece does. Off, recipes that already have lead still open as they were.
lead.warning: Use lead only as a frit, never as raw red, white or yellow lead or litharge. Mix it wet, never spray it, wear a respirator and clean up wet. Keep lead-glazed ware away from food and drink unless a laboratory leach test of the fired piece has passed.

on.label: Show the English after key terms
on.saved: Saved: the English shown after key terms.

englishTerms.help: For reading English sources, such as Digitalfire, beside this one: key terms get their English in brackets.

hidden.label: Hidden
hidden.saved: Saved: the notice is hidden. A line of it stays in the safety guides.
hidden.savedPlain: Saved: the notice is hidden. A line of it stays at the top of each page.

notice.help: The note at the top of each page saying it was translated by AI, with a way to suggest a correction.

confirmEmail.heading: Confirm your email
confirmEmail.intro: Press the button to confirm this address.
confirmEmail.incomplete: This page needs the link from a confirmation email, and this one is incomplete.
confirmEmail.failed: Error: could not confirm the address. Please try again.

tokens.heading: Access tokens
tokens.intro: An access token lets your own AI assistant or script read the recipes, materials, notes and firing logs in your account. For now a token can only read: it never changes or removes anything. Each token stops working on the day you choose, or as soon as you revoke it.
tokens.howTo: How to connect an AI assistant
tokens.revokeFailed: Error: could not revoke the token. Please try again.
tokens.loadFailed: Your access tokens could not be loaded. Please reload the page to try again.
tokens.name: Name
tokens.nameHint: Something to tell it apart by, such as the assistant or computer it is for.
tokens.nameCheck: Please give the token a name of 1 to {most} characters.
tokens.expiryHint: We email you 7 days before a token stops working.
tokens.scopeNote: The token can read your records but not change them.
tokens.confirmStep: To make the token, confirm it is you.
tokens.failed: Error: could not make the token. Please try again.
tokens.limit: You have {most} access tokens working, the most an account can have. Revoke one to make another.
tokens.newText: This is the only time it is shown. Anyone who has it can read your records until it stops working, so keep it like a password, and give it only to your own assistant or script.
tokens.copyFailed: Could not copy. Select the token and copy it yourself.
tokens.keptText: {count, plural, one {Changing your password did not stop your access token. If you changed it because someone else may know it, revoke the token too.} other {Changing your password did not stop your # access tokens. If you changed it because someone else may know it, revoke them too.}}
